title: Design Novelty Mining and Object Retrieval
prompt:
Design a system that selects novel, useful data from a huge unlabeled multimodal corpus and later retrieves items containing a requested object.

Define the selection and retrieval inputs and outputs. Explain how you would measure usefulness and novelty, incorporate human feedback, handle duplicates and updates, and evaluate retrieval quality. Discuss the trade-off between offline processing cost and online latency.

response.placeholder: Define novelty relative to a time and domain baseline, then separate offline discovery from online retrieval.
response.reference_answer:
## Offline discovery
Ingest versioned data, remove exact/near duplicates, calculate modality-appropriate representations, cluster by domain and time, and score candidates using rarity, distance to known coverage, and diversity constraints. Novelty is a hypothesis, not a scalar truth: sample candidates for human usefulness/quality labels and calibrate by domain.

## Online retrieval
Use an ANN index for high-recall candidate generation, then object detector/region or cross-modal reranker for precision. Keep corpus/version provenance so results are reproducible and filters can exclude unauthorized or deprecated data.

## Feedback and evaluation
Review labels feed active sampling and threshold calibration. Evaluate retrieval with recall, precision, and NDCG on held-out time splits; evaluate novelty by judged precision, diversity/coverage gain, duplicate leakage, reviewer cost, and freshness.

## Progressive Hints
1. A sparse cluster is not automatically useful.
2. Discovery and serving optimize different objectives.
3. Hold out time to avoid near-duplicate optimism.
